extracted.intended_audience: National LES societies, prospective LES100 instructors, and professionals new to IP licensing
extracted.subtask_description: An LESI-prescribed introductory course (LES 100) for people new to IP licensing, outlining required course content (five modules), teaching methods (exercises, interaction, mock negotiation), instructor qualifications and training, material use/confidentiality rules, and national society responsibilities for running the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course purpose and pedagogical format
rubrics_metrics.description: LES 100 is the introductory course in the Licensing Executives Society’s Intellectual Asset Management Series, designed for those who are relatively new to licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course provides attendees with an overview of intellectual property and licensing, divided into five modules, with examples, exercises, and interaction between instructors and fellow students including a mock licensing negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How a National Society conducts the course
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested LES chapters must contact the LESI Education Committee to run the course and will be provided a Course information package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Course information package will be made available to the member society, including access to the course materials for adaptation and/or translation to local law and requirements. The organisation, advertisement and pricing of the course is in the responsibility of the National LES Society. Member societies interested in hosting/offering the course must contact the LESI Education Committee or staff for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course materials access and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Course materials are provided to member societies for adaptation/translation but soft copies must be kept strictly confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soft copies of all course materials must be kept strictly confidential. There is an automatic grant back of a royalty free license of any adaptations and translations of the course materials to LESI and LES South Africa, and all adaptations and translations of the course material must be delivered to the LESI Education Committee or staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational guidelines and marketing/certificate templates provided
rubrics_metrics.description: The course information package includes organizational guidelines and templates for marketing material and certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These templates and organizational guidelines are included in the Course information package to assist National Societies in running the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor composition (number and complementary backgrounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is ideal to teach the course with at least 2 experienced instructors, one having a strong legal background and the other a strong commercial or business background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of qualified instructors is part of the course information package provided. It is recommended that National Societies build up their own qualified instructors group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualification and training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor candidates must first attend the LES100 course themselves and then participate in a Train the Trainer qualification workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor candidates have to attend the LES100 course once themselves and then take part in a half–day Train the Trainer course instructor qualification workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor status and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: LES 100 is designed to be delivered by LES volunteers who are active practitioners in their fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with all LES courses, LES 100 is designed to be delivered by LES volunteers who are active practitioners; a list of qualified instructors is available at the LESI Education Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module 1 — Introduction & IP Basics (content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce, define and give examples of the different types of IP in the context of commercialisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics to cover include patents, trademarks, copyright, designs and trade secrets in the context of commercialisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module 2 — Basics of IP Commercialisation & Licensing (content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an introduction to licensing and related commercial and legal concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reasons for licensing, description of licensing agreements, infringement, competition law, and relationship–building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module 3 — Determining Reasonable Licence Fees & Royalty Rates (content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach valuation approaches and royalty structures and discuss risks and rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover different valuation methods (Market, Financial, Cost) and their pros and cons, together with royalty structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module 4 — Managing Risks (content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify different kinds of risk relevant to licensing and how to manage them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address confidentiality, infringement, liability, collection of royalties and other fees, and techniques to manage these risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module 5 — Licensing Game (practical exercise requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a practical negotiation exercise where students apply what they have learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are divided into licensee and licensor teams to discuss and negotiate terms on a licensing case study; at the end all teams report their results and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course duration and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: LES 100 is designed to run over one full day or two half days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course format may be delivered as a single full day or split into two half-day sessions to suit local scheduling.
